gaps: P0: none; P4–P6: none usable (modern photos are all close-ups of doorways and statues)
notes: #1 and #4 (Braun and Hogenberg vol. 2, 1575, colored) are bound-book spreads with the fold running through the town, so I used Hogenberg’s loose 1574 siege sheet (#3) instead, marked as an event; swap in #4 if the fold is acceptable. #14’s title dates the view itself to 1744; the Rijksmuseum dates the print 1751–60, so I used that. #13 (1831) is faint and the town is small in the frame, but it is the only 19th-century view; #11 and #12 are other impressions of the same lithograph. #8 and #9 are reconstructions of the town as it was around 1400.
